conditions: The baseline and candidate use the same scenario prompt, fixture, sandbox profile, capability profile and deadline.

evals.prompt: The runnable project in evals/files/measurement-decisions exposes its real inventory HTTP endpoint and has a project-owned median latency gate but no universal performance target. Run the benchmark, gate and profiler, keep those decisions separate, find the dominant cost and make the smallest behavior-preserving optimization. Keep filtered output, ordering and the gate value unchanged. Report raw before/after samples and the ratio.
evals.expected_output: The response measures the real HTTP path before changing code, reports the benchmark samples separately from the project gate and profiler attribution, identifies repeated all-item scanning and profile work as the dominant cause, preserves duplicate removal, report fields, ordering and the project gate constant, and reports comparable raw samples, aggregates and a negative control.
assertions: The response measures the production HTTP endpoint rather than a copied benchmark algorithm.
The response reports benchmark samples, the project gate decision and profiler attribution as separate decisions.
The response identifies repeated all-item scanning and per-item profile work as the dominant cost.
The candidate preserves duplicate removal, report fields, ordering and the unchanged gate value.
The response reports raw before/after samples, an aggregate, a negative control and the ratio.
The edited project's focused test passes.

evals.prompt: Diagnose why editing one row in evals/files/stable-identity-subscription re-renders every row. Do not change code. State the smallest design that narrows the subscription while keeping row identity for unchanged rows, preserving update order and retaining the immediate initial event. Each scoped subscription must return an equivalent unsubscribe that removes its own listener without affecting the others. Include a falsifiable before/after check.

assertions: The response makes no production code change.

The response narrows delivery without changing row identity for unchanged rows.
The response preserves update order and the immediate initial event.
The proposed scoped subscription returns teardown that removes only its own listener.
The response includes a negative control that fails with the original subscription behavior.
The response keeps collection order and subscriber behavior explicit.
